My most recent experience was with the receptionist, Vijaya, and it was nothing short of appalling. When I asked for her surname in order to make a formal complaint, she flatly refused. She falsely told me that the practice manager had “left the surgery” and that no senior staff were available. When pressed, she pretended to check, only to return and claim that they were “in a meeting” and could not speak with me.

I then asked about blood test results which had been pending for more than two weeks. Her response was: “I don’t know who you spoke to. I don’t care. I didn’t speak to you. You should make a doctor’s appointment but I’m not going to give you anything.” She refused to provide any information whatsoever and then hung up on me.

This behaviour is utterly disgraceful. Patients should never be treated with such contempt, rudeness, and outright hostility; especially not in a GP surgery where compassion and professionalism are supposed to be the standard. After three decades as patients here, my family and I are left feeling ignored, disrespected, and deeply disappointed.
